```{python}
# Load data

# this function cleans up the weird column name formatting SQLAlchemy addes to the df when loading. 
def load_table(table_name, engine):
    df = pd.read_sql_table(table_name, engine)
    df.columns = [str(col) for col in df.columns]
    return df

dc_df = load_table("naics_518_establishments", engine)
air_df = load_table("air_quality", engine)
bus_df = load_table("business_patterns", engine)
gdp_df = load_table("gdp", engine)
inc_df = load_table("personal_income", engine)
pop_df = load_table("population", engine)
perm_df = load_table("res_construction_permits", engine)
emp_df = load_table("unemployment", engine)
county_df = load_table("us_counties", engine)
```

## Create Table for models

```{python}
# keep only 2022 (closest to when we know data center counts to be true)

df_with_years = [dc_df, air_df, bus_df, gdp_df, inc_df, pop_df, perm_df, emp_df]
dfs_only_2022 = [mlu.return_specific_year(x, 2022) for x in df_with_years]
```

```{python}
# Aggregate all industry codes per county into one summed row
dfs_only_2022[2] = dfs_only_2022[2].groupby(
    ["county_id"],
    as_index=False
    ).sum()

dfs_only_2022[2] = dfs_only_2022[2].drop(columns = ["naics_industry_code"])
```

```{python}
# Add column to county_df which indicates the presence of one or more data centers in a county
dc_df_2022 = dfs_only_2022[0]

counties_with_dc = dc_df_2022["county_id"].unique()

county_df["has_datacenter"] = county_df["county_id"].isin(counties_with_dc).astype(int)
county_df = county_df[[
    "county_id",
    "has_datacenter",
    "centroid_lon",
    "centroid_lat",
    "land_area_sqmi",
    "water_area_sqmi"
    ]]
```

```{python}
# combine all data together
mega_df = mlu.combine_dfs(county_df, dfs_only_2022[1:])
```


```{python}
# log all columns with lots of outliers
cols_to_log = list(set(mega_df.columns) - set(mlu.column_selector(mega_df, False, -1, 3, False, False)))

def log_cols(df, cols_to_log):
    for col in cols_to_log:
        df[col] = df[col].replace(0,1e-9) #logging a zero causes -inf
        df[f"{col}_logged"] = np.log(df[col])
        df = df.drop(columns=[col])
    return df

df_logged = log_cols(mega_df, cols_to_log)
```

```{python}
cols_no_crazy_outliers = mlu.column_selector(df_logged, False, -1, 5, False, False)
df_trimmed_cols = df_logged[cols_no_crazy_outliers]
df_trimmed_cols = df_trimmed_cols.dropna()
```


```{python}
X = df_trimmed_cols.drop('has_datacenter', axis=1)
y = df_trimmed_cols['has_datacenter']

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
```


```{python}

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_scaled, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_train_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_pca = pca.transform(X_test)

smote = SMOTE(sampling_strategy='minority', random_state=57)
```

### UMAP

```{python}
# un-supervised
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=2000, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42)
X_train_umap = reducer.fit_transform(X_train)

X_test_umap = reducer.transform(X_test)

# plot training data
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
scatter = plt.scatter(
    X_train_umap[:, 0], 
    X_train_umap[:, 1], 
    c=y_train, 
    cmap='coolwarm', 
    edgecolor='k', 
    s=80,
    alpha = 0.3
)
plt.xlabel('UMAP Dimension 1')
plt.ylabel('UMAP Dimension 2')
plt.title('UMAP Projection of Training Data')
plt.colorbar(scatter, label='Target classes')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# plot testing data
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
scatter = plt.scatter(
    X_test_umap[:, 0], 
    X_test_umap[:, 1], 
    c=y_test, 
    cmap='coolwarm', 
    edgecolor='k', 
    s=80,
    alpha = 0.3
)
plt.xlabel('UMAP Dimension 1')
plt.ylabel('UMAP Dimension 2')
plt.title('UMAP Projection of Test Data')
plt.colorbar(scatter, label='Target classes')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

